answer.rationale: p99 latency is climbing on the write path, a release went out 2 hours ago, and writes are heavy at settlement peak. memory_b1 documents that rolling back the prior build cleared a checkout error spike with no customer impact. memory_b4 documents circuit breakers preserving the checkout path by failing fast. Pulling the archive for b1 confirms whether the rollback procedure was safe under heavy write load before; b4 confirms the breaker behavior so we know writes will fail fast rather than queue if the rollback itself stumbles. With a budget of one intervention, rollback is the highest-leverage move: it directly addresses the most likely regression source while preserving the write path through the fail-fast discipline in b4. Regional failover and read-replica routing do not help the write path, and adding capacity does not fix a regression. If the archive review of b1 surfaces a reason the rollback cannot be done safely under today's peak, I will fall back to enabling the breaker from b4 to shed load and protect writes until the next window.
